name: T-Motor F60 Pro IV V2.0 1950KV
notes: T-Motor's own page (https://uav-en.tmotor.com/html/2020/FPV_0424/374.html) no longer resolves, and retailers carry two revisions with different numbers; this record is the V2.0, whose set is complete and self-consistent. Retailer spec list: "KV 1950", 12N14P, "Size (H * W) 26.8mm * 32.7mm", "Shaft diameter 5mm", "Holes 4x16mm M3", "Weight (with cable) 33.4g", "Impedance 60mΩ" (winding resistance), "Maximum current 42A", "Maximum power 949W", "Voltage 6S". Stator 22 x 7.5 mm from the 2207.5 model name. Prop thread M5, as the 5 mm shaft. Idle current: TODO(source), not published for the V2.0 (the motor model runs without an idle loss). No thrust test with RPM was found, and T-Motor publishes no recommended propeller list on that page, so recommendedProps is empty. The earlier record (32.4 g, 55 mΩ, 1000 W, 1.2 A idle, 27.5 x 33.5 mm) matched neither revision. This is a 6S motor; on a 4S pack it simply runs slower.

name: Sunnysky X2216-III 880KV
notes: Manufacturer page (X2216-III): KV880, stator 22 x 16 mm, rotor diameter "27.7mm", "Motor length: 34mm", shaft "3.175mm" (a prop adapter is included, so no prop-shaft size is given), "67.5g", "89mΩ", no-load "0.5A/10V", "30A/30s", "440W", 3-4S, ESC 50A, recommended props "APC9047, APC9045, APC11*4.7, APC1047" (none of them is in this dataset, so recommendedProps is empty). Its test table includes the APC 9x6 ("APC9060") at 14.8 V: top row 19.9 A, 1290 g, 294.52 W, 10547 RPM. Mount pattern: TODO(source). The earlier record (72 g, 75 mΩ, 28 A, 450 W, 0.8 A, 4 mm shaft) mixed in the older X2216 (II) page (http://en.rcsunnysky.com/x-fixedwingseries/1102.html: 72 g, 117 mΩ) and unsourced values; the old sunnysky-motor.com URL does not resolve.

name: BrotherHobby VY 1504.5 3950KV
notes: There is no "Avenger 1504.5"; BrotherHobby's 1504.5 is the VY 1504.5, sold in "2650KV(4S)/2950KV(6S)/3950KV(4S)" (product page; the old URL now shows an unrelated product). Every number here is from BrotherHobby's VY 1504.5-3950KV test report image on that page (https://ueeshop.ly200-cdn.com/u_file/UPAH/UPAH113/2409/photo/518befd6d3.jpg): 3950KV, 12N14P, stator 15 x 4.5 mm, "Weight Including Cable (g)" 12.07, "Motor Dimension (mm)" Φ19.2x19.5, 4S, propeller "3in", "Internal Resistance(mΩ)" 139.74, "Idle Current@5V (A)" 0.67, "Max power (W)" 211.20 and "Max Current (A)" 13.20 (the 100 % point of its load test, not a continuous rating), Ø1.5 mm shaft, 4-M2 mounting holes on a Ø12 mm circle. Load test with "GF 3016 Triblade" at 16.00 V, 100 %: 13.20 A, 48782 RPM, 454 g. It is a 3-inch motor; no 3-inch propeller is in this dataset, so recommendedProps is empty. The earlier record's 115 mΩ, 18 A, 288 W, 0.6 A and 5 mm prop shaft were not published anywhere.

name: Sunnysky V4008 380KV Flat Multirotor
notes: Corrected against the manufacturer page (the old sunnysky-motor.com URL does not resolve): KV380, 18N24P, stator 39 x 8 mm, φ44.3 x 21 mm, 4.0 mm shaft, 105 g with wire, 131 mΩ, no-load 0.5 A @ 10 V, 500 W and 20 A / 30 s maximum continuous, 4-6S, recommended EOLO CN12x5 / CN13x5 / CN15x5.5 / CN17x6.2. The earlier record said 93 g, 105 mΩ, 0.4 A idle and a 6 mm shaft. mountCircle_mm (25) is not stated on the page and is unverified. recommendedProps is empty: the page recommends EOLO CN12x5 / CN13x5 / CN15x5.5 / CN17x6.2, none of which is linked to this motor's own test in the dataset (the earlier list named APC and Master Airscrew props the page does not mention).

name: GEPRC GR1404 4500KV
notes: Manufacturer page: "KV: 4500", 9N12P, stator 14 mm x 4 mm, "Shaft Diameter: 1.5mm", "Motor Dimensions: Φ18.3 * 14.5mm", "The hole position of motor：9mm", "Weight: 9.8g", "Idle current@8V(A) ≤0。51" (an upper bound at 8 V, used as the idle current), "Max Continuous Power(180S): 214", "Max Current(180S): 13.38A", 2-4S. The page prints "Internal Resistance: 0.213mΩ"; 0.213 mΩ is physically impossible for a 1404 winding, so it is read as 0.213 Ω = 213 mΩ (GEPRC's sister SPEEDX2 1404 lists "Interphase resistance: 0.19Ω"). The CineLog25 V2 page names its motor "SPEEDX 1404 4500KV"; GEPRC sells no standalone motor by that name, and the GR1404 is GEPRC's only 1404 at 4500 KV, so this record is the closest published match, not a confirmed part number. No recommended propeller is published, so recommendedProps is empty.

name: iFlight XING2 2809 1250KV
notes: From iFlight's test-report image on the product page (https://shop.iflight.com/image/catalog/TEST%20REPORT/XING2-2809-1250KV.png): 1250KV, "Weight (included wire) 60.7g", φ35.33 x 36.7 mm, interphase resistance 65.46 mΩ, input 24 V, peak current 50 A, max watt 1145 W, 19x19 mm M3 mount, 5 mm shaft, 12N14P. Stator 28 x 9 mm is read from the model number (the industry naming convention), not a published dimension. maxCurrent_A is the published PEAK current; no continuous rating is published. Idle current: TODO(source), not published, so the motor model runs with no idle loss. Thrust test at 24 V with "GF 7040" at 100%: 23.56 V, 30.36 A, 2092 g, 715.28 W (and HQ 8x4x3: 23.30 V, 49.23 A, 2933 g).

name: T-Motor MN4014 330KV (Navigator)
notes: Manufacturer page: KV330, 18N24P, stator 40 x 14 mm, Φ44.7 x 34.5 mm, 4 mm shaft, 171 g with cables (150 g without), internal resistance 85 mΩ, idle current 1.1 A @ 10 V, max continuous 25 A (180 s), max power 750 W (180 s), 4-8S, recommended prop "T-MOTOR P17*5.8". Mount: 4-M3 on Ø25 mm (technical drawing on the same page); props bolt to a 12 mm two-hole pattern, not over the shaft. Test table at 22.2 V with 17x5.8 CF, 100% throttle: 17 A, 377.40 W, 2600 g, 5400 RPM. The page's highlights also say "Max. thrust:3.3kg", which disagrees with its own 2.6 kg table; the table is what the propeller record is derived from.

name: Sunnysky X4112S 450KV
notes: Manufacturer page (XS multirotor series): "X4112S/ KV450", 12N14P, "Internal resistance" "43mΩ", "Motor size" "φ47.5*33.5mm", "Shaft diameter" "4.0mm", "Motor weight(wire included)" "169g", 6S, "No-load current" "0.7A/10V", "Maximum continuous power" "1950W", "Maximum continuous current" "78A/30s" (a 30-second rating), "ESC recommended use" "80A", recommended props "EOLO CN13*5 15*5.5 16*6"; stator 41 mm x 12 mm. Mount pattern and prop adapter are not stated in the page text: TODO(source). Test table with EOLO CN13*5 at 22.2 V, 100 %: 27.9 A, 3020 g, 619.38 W, 8978 RPM. Used as the VTBIRD's lift motor: Finwing's combo names an "X4112S KV485", which Sunnysky does not list (its X4112S comes in KV340, 400 and 450) and whose numbers are not published, so the closest published winding, KV450, stands in for it.

name: Sunnysky X3520-III 560KV
notes: Manufacturer page (X fixed-wing series): "X3520-III/ KV560", 12N14P, "Internal resistance" "23mΩ", "Motor size" "φ42.5*64.0mm" (body length 45 mm; 64 mm includes the shaft), "Shaft diameter" "5.0mm", "Motor weight(wire included)" "219g", 6S, "No-load current" "1.1A/10V", "Rated power 880W", "Rated current 40A" (the page gives rated, not peak, figures: these are maxPower_W and maxCurrent_A), ESC 60-80A, recommended props "APC12*8/APC12*6/APC13*6.5/APC13*8/APC14*7"; stator 35 mm x 20 mm. Mount pattern: TODO(source), not in the page text. Its own test table with APC14*7 at 22.2 V reaches 66.6 A and 4430 g at 100 %, far past the 40 A rating, so this app's motor model holds it to 40 A. The XUWING VTBIRD 4+1 power combo names this motor ("Sunnysky X3520 III KV 560") as its pusher.

name: KDE Direct KDE3510XF-475
notes: Replaces the old "KDE3512XF-400" record: KDE Direct sells no such motor (its URL is dead) and its numbers were not published anywhere. Manufacturer page: "475 RPM/V", "3510" stator, 12N14P, "ф42.2 mm" x "35 mm", "120 g (175 g with Wires/Bullets)" (175 g used, as the other records weigh motors with their wires), shaft "ф4 mm (ф5 mm Internal)" with an "XF UAS M6 x 17mm Propeller Adapter" (so the prop bore it takes is 6 mm), mounting "M4/3 x ф25 mm, M3/2.5 x ф32 mm", "0.105 Ω", "Io (@10V) 0.2 A", "30 A (180 s)", "665 W (180 s)", "14.8 V (4S LiPo) - 26.1 V (6S LiHV)", for "15.5\" x 5.3 Dual-Propeller Blades" (not in this dataset, so recommendedProps is empty). Stator height 10 mm from the 3510 model name. It is in the dataset as the heavy-lift motor: on a 5-inch propeller it cannot lift a quad, which the physics check asserts.
